back: Moral principles guiding businesses to do what is right and fair, not only what is legal or profitable.
Taking responsibility for the effects of business decisions on society and the environment, beyond legal requirements.
Fair wages and conditions, child labour, fair prices to suppliers, honest advertising, bribery, the environment (and tax).
Reputation, customer loyalty, motivated staff, attracts investors, avoids fines and boycotts.
Higher costs, possibly higher prices, lower short-term profit, may be undercut by rivals.
The law is the minimum; some legal actions are still unethical (e.g. underpaying powerless suppliers).
A written code of conduct setting out how employees should behave.
Community projects (boreholes, classrooms), staff training, recycling, buying locally, health programmes.
